request.spec:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A fourth role, restricted, can be assigned. A restricted user sees on the people list only the
people of the crews they lead or belong to (by a person with the user's name) and that person
themselves: no other row is on the screen. Every other figure (the totals row, the header, the
summary, the periods, the pools) is still over everyone on the sheet.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
I added the restricted role, and all 4 acceptance tests pass with `bin/e2e`.

**Server (`role/`)**
- `Role.java` has a new `RESTRICTED = "restricted"` value.
- `ValidateRole` now accepts restricted. Any other unknown role (like "x") is still refused, and its error message lists the four roles.
- A restricted user can otherwise make changes like a clerk. Only viewers are blocked from changing things.

**Front end**
- `features/people/list.slot.tsx` decides which rows are shown. A restricted user sees only:
  - the person with their name, matched the same way the header matches a user to a person (name or alias, ignoring case);
  - the lead and members of every crew that person leads or belongs to.
- If no person has the user's name, a restricted user sees no rows.
- To avoid briefly showing rows they shouldn't see, the list stays empty until the roles, delegations and crews have loaded.
- The role checked is the one the user acts in. So a restricted user who has been delegated steward sees everyone while the delegation lasts.
- The filter only hides rows. The totals row, header, summary, periods and pools still count everyone, because they work from the full people list.
- The roles form placeholder and error text now mention restricted.

**One fix outside the request:** the header's "My due" (`my-due-total`) showed "0.00" for a person whose due-total is "n/a". The test expects "n/a", matching what that person's row shows. It now uses the person's own figure (`features/header/counters.slot.tsx`), which only changes the result when the figure is "n/a". "My overdue" works as before.

No stored data or schema changed, because roles are already kept as free text.
